nodes.author: AuthenticThoz
nodes.text: @yabaleftonline Human Metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a respiratory virus that primarily affects the respiratory tract. It belongs to the Paramyxoviridae family and was first identified in 2001. It is closely related to the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)

nodes.author: AuthenticThoz
nodes.text:
@yabaleftonline Prevention
Good hand hygiene.
Avoid close contact with infected individuals.
Disinfect surfaces frequently.
No vaccine is currently available.

nodes.author: AuthenticThoz
nodes.text:
@yabaleftonline No specific antiviral therapy exists.

Management focuses on supportive care, such as hydration, fever management, and oxygen therapy in severe cases.

nodes.author: AuthenticThoz
nodes.text:
@yabaleftonline Mild cases: Cough, runny nose, sore throat, and fever.

Severe cases: Bronchiolitis, pneumonia, difficulty breathing, and wheezing.

nodes.author: AuthenticThoz
nodes.text:
@yabaleftonline Primarily affects young children, the elderly, and individuals with weakened immune systems.

Healthy adults can also contract the virus but usually experience milder symptoms.

nodes.author: AuthenticThoz
nodes.text: @yabaleftonline HMPV spreads through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes, or through direct contact with contaminated surfaces.

nodes.author: AuthenticThoz
